You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network API gateway is down: pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx runs container nginx-thrift with resources.requests.memory=16Mi and limits.memory=16Mi, is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137) and is the only one of the 27 social-network pods that is not Ready, so Service nginx-thrift has no ready endpoint and the gateway stops serving (no nginx-web-server traces after 2026-11-24T09:24:54.876Z). Its own Deployment (revision 2) and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 declare 128Mi requests / 256Mi limits, while the other 26 social-network pods, created at 09:24:27Z-09:24:31Z, carry no resource limits at all; the only pod carrying exactly the 16Mi value is the one created at 09:24:56Z. At 09:24:47Z a Deployment platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops was created running /app/server.py as an HTTPS admission server, and at 09:24:48Z five MutatingWebhookConfigurations were created that all send pod admissions for namespace social-network to platform-policy-controller.platform-ops:443/mutate. The ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server holds that server's code with MEMORY = "16Mi" and a patch builder that stamps requests.memory and limits.memory=16Mi onto container[0]. The evidence therefore points to this admission webhook as the origin of the 16Mi limit that kills the gateway, though the injected patch itself was not directly observed. Node memory pressure is ruled out (all node pressure conditions false at 09:25:00Z).

claims.text: The Deployment platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops was created 2026-11-24T09:24:47Z (generation 1, last write by manager kubectl-client-side-apply) and its pod platform-policy-controller-7d44bbdc6b-5x6tl (created 09:24:47Z) is Running with image python:3.12-alpine.

The Deployment platform-policy-controller runs container 'webhook' with command ["python","/app/server.py"] mounted from ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server, exposes containerPort 8443, and is fronted by Service platform-policy-controller (ClusterIP, port 443 -> targetPort 8443, selector app=platform-policy-controller).

ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in namespace platform-ops contains server.py with MEMORY = "16Mi" and a build_patch() function that emits RFC6902 'add' operations writing resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory = 16Mi on container[0] of the admitted Pod, returned as a JSONPatch AdmissionReview response.

All five MutatingWebhookConfigurations present (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) have clientConfig.service = platform-policy-controller / namespace platform-ops / port 443 / path /mutate and namespaceSelector matching kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network; the rule for gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration (webhook mutation.gatekeeper.sh) applies to core/v1 pods on CREATE. All five were created 2026-11-24T09:24:48Z.

An event at 2026-11-24T09:24:47Z records for involvedObject Endpoints platform-policy-controller (namespace platform-ops): reason FailedToCreateEndpoint, message 'Failed to create endpoint for service platform-ops/platform-policy-controller: endpoints "platform-policy-controller" already exists'.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx was created 2026-11-24T09:24:56Z and its container nginx-thrift has resources.requests.memory=16Mi and resources.limits.memory=16Mi; it is the only one of the 27 social-network pods with any resources set — the other 26 pods (created 09:24:27Z-09:24:31Z, before the webhook server existed) have no requests or limits.

The 16Mi value is not declared by the workload: Deployment nginx-thrift (revision 2) and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 both declare the nginx-thrift container with resources.requests.memory=128Mi and limits.memory=256Mi, while the pod of that same ReplicaSet carries 16Mi, so the low limit was applied to the Pod, not taken from its controller template.

Container nginx-thrift in pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx is failing by OOM kill: lastState.terminated.reason=OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 09:25:18Z (an earlier instance exited 137/reason Error at 09:25:04Z), restartCount rose from 2 to 3, current state is terminated/waiting with ready=false, and pod condition Ready=False reason=ContainersNotReady; Deployment nginx-thrift reports availableReplicas=null.
The Service nginx-thrift (port 8080) has no ready backend at query time: its single endpoint subset lists pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx (10.244.234.188) only under notReadyAddresses.

Traces of service nginx-web-server (operations /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read, /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read with http.status_code=200) exist only up to start time 1795512294875000 (2026-11-24T09:24:54.875Z); the newest trace returned for the window is 2026-11-24T09:24:54.876470Z, and a search restricted to 09:24:50Z-09:25:07Z returned only spans starting at or before that time.

Node-level memory pressure and eviction are ruled out as the reason nginx-thrift was killed: at 09:25:00Z kube_node_status_condition shows MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all equal to 0 for sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3.

A namespace-wide default limit or ResourceQuota is ruled out as the source of the 16Mi: the query for ResourceQuota objects in namespace social-network returned no objects, and 26 of 27 pods in the namespace have no resources set at all, whereas a namespace-wide default would have applied to every pod.

The 16Mi memory limit that kills nginx-thrift was injected by the admission webhook served by Deployment platform-policy-controller: the pod created at 09:24:56Z, after the webhook Deployment/Service (09:24:47Z) and the five webhook configurations (09:24:48Z), carries exactly that server's MEMORY constant (16Mi on container[0], both requests and limits), while its controller template says 128Mi/256Mi and pre-webhook pods carry nothing; 16Mi is far below what the OpenResty gateway needs, so the container is OOM-killed and the gateway loses all ready endpoints.

The blast radius is likely wider than nginx-thrift: because gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration (mutation.gatekeeper.sh) matches every pod CREATE in namespace social-network with failurePolicy Fail, any future pod replacement in that namespace (container[0] of each workload) should receive the same 16Mi limit. No other workload has been observed failing with this signature yet.

Disable and delete the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations whose clientConfig points at platform-policy-controller.platform-ops:443/mutate, delete Deployment/Service platform-policy-controller and ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in platform-ops, then delete pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx so its replacement is admitted with the Deployment's 128Mi/256Mi resources; audit the identity that used kubectl-client-side-apply at 09:24:47Z and check webhook registrations in other namespaces.

gaps: No admission/audit log was available showing the webhook's AdmissionReview response applying the 16Mi patch to nginx-thrift-65f656c999-5dpnx; the inference rests on the matching 16Mi constant, the creation order (webhooks 09:24:47-48Z, pod 09:24:56Z) and the controller template saying 256Mi.

The change_history integration is not connected, and managedFieldsSummary only records the last write per manager, so when and by whom the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations and the ConfigMap were changed cannot be established.

data.server.py:
import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain("/certs/tls.crt", "/certs/tls.key")
httpd.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(httpd.socket, server_side=True)
httpd.serve_forever()
